title: Lesson 3: Stack Implementation using Linked List

content.text: Hello! In the last lesson, we saw that array stacks are fast but limited by a fixed maximum size. Today, we will build a stack using a **Linked List** to allow the stack to grow dynamically to any size we want. Let's do it!
Instead of pre-allocating an array block, we create list nodes dynamically on-demand. Each node has a `val` storage slot and a `next` address pointer.
To achieve $O(1)$ constant time for both push and pop operations, we always insert and delete elements at the **Head** of the linked list. The `top` pointer is simply the head node pointer!

content.question: Why is insertion and deletion done at the head node in a linked-list stack?
options: To achieve constant O(1) time complexity for both push and pop.
Because it is impossible to insert at the tail.
